title: v0.0.1
items: ESP32 configured
E-Ink display working
First UI rendered
Yes, I know, I soldered the pins in the wrong direction. I fixed it later.

title: Front lid Prototype 1
items: First enclosure top cover printed
Learned enclosure is too small for PCB
Screw holes tested, quite small

images.alt: Many tries of the front panel

title: Front lid Prototype 2
items: Fits well, but it sits on top of the PCB and needs to be made slightly over the edge.

title: Front lid Prototype 3
items: Fits well, but I still need to adjust the back part to have a good grid for the PCB and edges.

title: Front lid Prototype 4
items: Almost perfect, maybe I will adjust the size a bit more.
In the future, I might make it deeper.

title: First button
items: First button input succeeded!
And don't forget: BUTTONS HAVE ORIENTATION!
Then I connected the display as well and added a function which refreshes the display.
When I click the button, the screen refreshes.

title: v0.0.2
items: First button connected to pin 0
GUI refreshment
Renamed happiness to fun so in GUI it is displayed as F instead of a second H

title: Button functions
items: The button now feeds the monster by 10 until hunger is back to 0.

title: New GUI
items: I updated the GUI to look a bit cleaner and polished. Obviously, it is not final yet.
I also had to rename happiness to fun so there are not two H values displayed; it was quite confusing.
I am considering changing it later to something like HUN, ENG, FUN, AGE or just using icons.

title: Three buttons connected
items: Connected two more buttons and added them on pins 8, 9 and 10.
The old Feed button was removed, and currently the code only prints which button was pressed: LEFT, MIDDLE or RIGHT.
The breadboard is a mess, I know, but it will eventually be better.
Left button feeds the monster: hunger decreases by 10.
Middle button plays with the monster: fun increases by 10, hunger increases by 10, and energy decreases by 5.
Right button makes the monster sleep: fun decreases by 5, hunger increases by 5, and energy increases by 10.

title: v0.0.3
items: Added flash storage system
It was quite easy actually, so I am happy about that.
Saving is performed after a button is pressed.
I would also like to add an autosave every 5 minutes.

title: v0.0.4 - Audio System
items: Soldered speaker to MAX98357A amplifier.
Wired amplifier to ESP32-C3.
Created audio module (audio.hpp and audio.cpp).
The speaker produces buzz instead of a clear tone and I have no idea why; maybe the I2S config is wrong.

title: Audio update
items: Finally managed to implement clear sound with a specific configuration.
The problem was not the hardware but the audio config; wiring can stay as it is.
You can hear one beep sound when you power the device.

title: v0.0.5
items: I decided to switch to a new ESP32 module, the ESP32-S3, mostly because of the extra GPIO pins I will need for the accelerometer.
Currently waiting for the module to arrive (approx. 2 weeks).

title: UI and Menu System
items: Added a basic menu when the middle button is pressed.
The user can navigate using the left button, right button and middle button to confirm.

images.alt: What's on menu for today v0

title: Menu system update
items: Added a more polished menu system and made the code more readable and organized.
Settings are still mock, but I will implement them later. The user should be able to turn off the sound and change the monster name.
Next focus is monster logic.

title: v0.0.6
items: Added basic monster logic; the monster has different states and moods.
States: None, Playing, Eating, Sleeping, Dizzy, Sick, Injured, Dead.
Moods: Happy, Normal, Hungry, Tired, Bored, Sad, Critical.
It still needs testing. Not all states are implemented yet; for example, Dizzy logic will be added when the accelerometer is added.

title: Species
items: I am trying to add species, starting with Slime and Blob.

title: New menu entry
items: Added a new menu entry, Info, which displays more information about the monster itself: Name, Species and Status.
The status is currently None because the monster is alive and healthy. I don't want to show short-term status there, only long-term ones.
In the future I want to add an option to reset the monster.
I also increased the sleep and entertainment gain because it was too low.

images.alt: What's on menu for today v1

title: New ESP board struggle
items: It has been some time since I last worked on this project, but the new ESP finally arrived!
I tried switching to the new ESP32-S3 Super Mini board, but what a pain that was!

After about 3 hours of debugging, arguing with ChatGPT, and almost losing my mind, I ended up creating a custom configuration for this board since none of the available ESP32-S3 configs in PlatformIO were working.
The best part is that it works! Or at least I can see the === MONBIT === log.
The question is whether it's going to work with all the peripherals connected, but that's a TODO for now.
quote: Just a quick note: I wanted to use AI as little as possible, but yeah... here we go.
